subject: City Council Ward Representation Research
overview: The committee reviewed subcommittee research on Medford's demographics and historical representation before debating the merits of moving to a hybrid ward-based City Council. They tabled a decision on recommending council composition changes until November to allow for further public outreach.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the minutes from the previous meeting.

items.title: Council Composition Subcommittee Report
items.summary: A subcommittee presented its research on options for restructuring the City Council, comparing the current seven-member at-large model to various hybrid ward-based systems.

items.title: Demographic Analysis by Ward
items.summary: Jean Zotter detailed city demographics, highlighting that one ward is a minority-majority district and examining levels of language diversity across Medford.

items.title: Historical Representation Data
items.summary: Analysis of the last nine elections showed that residents of Wards 1 and 4 have not been elected to the City Council, whereas other wards are consistently over-represented.

items.title: Legal Case Studies and Structural Debate
items.summary: The committee reviewed a Voting Rights Act lawsuit in Lowell that forced a change to ward representation and debated a list of pros and cons regarding neighborhood-specific advocacy.

items.title: Decision on Council Structure Recommendation
items.summary: Tabled the final decision on recommending a council composition model until November to incorporate feedback from upcoming public sessions.

items.title: Community Listening Sessions Plan
items.summary: The committee approved a plan to host informal listening sessions in each ward and at community centers to gather feedback from underrepresented groups.

items.title: Public Forum Logistics
items.summary: Finalized plans for an October 19th public information session at City Hall, including the preparation of translated materials and a demographic presentation.

items.title: Interview and Survey Updates
items.summary: The committee reviewed the status of outstanding official interviews and noted that the city charter survey had received approximately 400 responses.
